item.title: Introduction to Apache Spark & Big Data
item.description:
1.1 What is Big Data?

➤ Definition:

Big Data refers to datasets that are too large or complex to be processed by traditional data processing tools (e.g., Excel, single-machine Python scripts).

➤ Characteristics (The 3 Vs + more):

V Description
Volume Huge amounts of data (TBs, PBs)
Velocity Fast data generation & processing (e.g., real-time logs)
Variety Structured, unstructured, and semi-structured data
Veracity Trustworthiness of the data
Value Insights extracted from the data

➤ Common Examples:

  • Logs from millions of devices
  • Financial transaction data
  • Clickstreams from web traffic
  • Social media feeds

1.2 Traditional vs Distributed Systems

Aspect Traditional Tools Distributed Systems (e.g., Spark)
Scale Single machine Cluster of machines
Fault Tolerance Weak Strong (data replicated across nodes)
Performance Bottlenecked by hardware Scales with more machines
Examples Pandas, Excel, R Spark, Hadoop, Dask, Flink

1.3 Overview of Apache Spark

➤ What is Apache Spark?

Apache Spark is an open-source, distributed computing engine designed for large-scale data processing and analytics. It has become the de facto engine for big data analytics in many industries due to its speed, scalability, and ease of use.
